html:
The Sultanate of Damagaram was a Muslim state centred on the city of Zinder, in what is now south-eastern Niger, from about 1731 to 1899. The map shows it in its 1880 snapshot, near its peak.

Damagaram began as a vassal of Bornu, on the borderland between Bornu and the Hausa city-states. In the 1800s it grew strong on the trans-Saharan trade: caravans from Zinder crossed the desert to Tripoli with ivory, ostrich feathers, hides and slaves. Sultan Tanimoun, who ruled for much of the mid-1800s, built up an army with guns and even locally made cannon, and expanded the state.

Damagaram resisted the French. After a French officer was killed in Zinder in 1898, a French column took the city in 1899. Zinder served as the capital of French Niger until 1926.
